name: Environmental_Demo
description: 30-second canyon walkthrough with geology, clouds, and education

questions.question: Can the player identify rock types from visual cues alone?
questions.answer: Only with the env_education module active. The geology module exists but needs to be wired to player triggers.

questions.question: Does the player learn to predict weather from cloud formations?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs weather-observer trigger that fires env_education.weather_prompt() on weather state change.

questions.question: Can curiosity-driven players discover deeper geology facts?
questions.answer: Partially. deep_geology_observation() exists but needs a scanner tool or examine action to trigger.

questions.question: Does the environment teach something the player uses later in gameplay?
questions.answer: Not yet designed. Possible: basalt = volcanic activity (resources), limestone = caves (shelter), flat-bottom clouds = stable weather (flight).

questions.question: What single screenshot makes a Steam shopper wishlist?
questions.answer: A canyon with visible rock strata + volumetric clouds + a single educational prompt overlay. One image shows all three systems working.

questions.question: How does this demo compare to No Man Sky environmental shots?
questions.answer: No Man Sky has more colors but zero education. Our differentiator: every rock, cloud, and star teaches something real.

questions.question: Could this demo be a 30-second Steam trailer?
questions.answer: Yes. 30-second trailer: canyon -> strata -> clouds -> learn geology -> day/night -> stars -> title card.

questions.question: What mechanic would a journalist call innovative here?
questions.answer: The scanner. Point at rock, learn geology. Point at cloud, learn meteorology. No game does this.

questions.question: Do clouds cast shadows that move across the terrain?
questions.answer: UVolumetricCloudComponent supports shadow casting. Property needs to be enabled.

questions.question: Does wind direction match cloud movement?
questions.answer: Not yet. The wind system and cloud system are independent. They need to be connected via the weather component.

questions.question: Can the player see the same constellation from different locations?
questions.answer: Yes, because the star sphere (SM_StarSphere) is world-aligned, not camera-aligned. A player at two different locations on the same planet sees the same star positions shifted by parallax. Different latitudes see different constellations — teaching celestial navigation naturally.

questions.question: Does day/night affect which educational observations appear?
questions.answer: Not yet. Education module generates time-of-day observations but is not wired to the day/night cycle in UE5.

questions.question: Can this demo be built and run without pipeline errors?
questions.answer: Not without fixing 5+ compiler errors in generated code. Each fix is 1-5 lines in the generator.

questions.question: What is the minimum UE5 compile fix needed?
questions.answer: Fix RespirationTimer undeclared identifier in generator. One 2-line change in game_code_generator.py.

questions.question: Does the demo run at 30fps on target hardware?
questions.answer: Unknown. Splat renderer not benchmarked with volumetric clouds. Needs telemetry probe.

questions.question: Can the demo be packaged as a standalone build?
questions.answer: Yes, UE5 supports standalone packaging. Blocked by same compile issue as Q14.

questions.question: Are MCP tools reliable enough for repeated actor spawning?
questions.answer: Yes. Tested: mcp_spawn_actor, mcp_capture_viewport, mcp_set_camera all succeeded.

questions.question: Does the worker bridge handle concurrent UE5 commands?
questions.answer: Not tested. Bridge processes sequentially. Concurrent MCP calls need queuing.

questions.question: Can the forge build UE5 content or only Python?
questions.answer: Currently Python-only. The forge builder can be extended with a UE5 compile stage when generator bugs are fixed.

questions.question: What is the graph query performance at 3000+ nodes?
questions.answer: Fast. Feature JSON lookup is O(1). Knowledge graph search is ~50ms over 4.3MB.

questions.question: Does this depend on the geology module (core/geology.py)?
questions.answer: Yes. core/geology.py is required for strata and rock type descriptions.

questions.question: Does this depend on the volumetric cloud actor being spawned?
questions.answer: Yes. The VolumetricCloud actor must exist in the level.

questions.question: Does this depend on the env_education module being wired to UE5?
questions.answer: Yes. Python functions exist but need generator or MCP trigger volume to appear in-game.

questions.question: Does this prove that MCP tools can build game content reliably?
questions.answer: Yes. Spawning clouds, placing cameras, capturing viewport all succeeded via MCP.

questions.question: Does this prove that educational mechanics can exist without a separate UI?
questions.answer: Not yet proven. Prompts need to be wired to HUD message or world-space text in UE5.

questions.question: Was this derived from the internal council on environmental systems?
questions.answer: Yes. The environmental council cycle produced the spec for geology + clouds + education.

questions.question: Does this conflict with the current pipeline compile errors?
questions.answer: No direct conflict. The pipeline errors are in other generated files, not in the environment systems.

questions.question: What UE5 knowledge is required to configure volumetric cloud properties?
questions.answer: Basic UE5 actor property knowledge. Set LayerBottomAltitude, LayerHeight, CloudDensity, CloudAlbedo via MCP.

questions.question: Does an environmental demo make the game more famous than a gameplay demo would?
questions.answer: Yes. Steam shoppers judge by screenshots. A canyon + clouds + education screenshot generates more wishlists than a UI screenshot.

questions.question: What features are NOT being built while we build this demo?
questions.answer: NPC systems (Loop 5), shelter (Loop 6), travel (Loop 7) — all deferred. The demo is the marketing asset.

questions.question: What evidence exists that environmental realism drives Steam sales?
questions.answer: No Man Sky sold 10M+ on planet screenshots. Subnautica marketed entirely on beautiful ocean. Education is our differentiator.

questions.question: Does this chain reach a human who plays the game, or just satisfy an architectural goal?
questions.answer: Yes. Steam shopper sees screenshot, reads learn geology, wishlists. That is a human terminal.

questions.question: Does this work in UE5.8 without hacks or workarounds?
questions.answer: Yes. The demo uses existing UE5.8 features: VolumetricCloudComponent, landscape spawning, and MCP bridge. No engine forks or plugins beyond McpAutomationBridge which is already compiled.

questions.question: Does this run at 30+ fps on the target GPU (RTX 3060)?
questions.answer: Unknown without telemetry. The splat renderer + volumetric clouds together have not been benchmarked. Need a probe.

questions.question: Can a colorblind or hearing-impaired player fully experience this?
questions.answer: Partially. Text-based educational prompts need screen reader support. Color-coded geology layers need patterns as fallback.

questions.question: Does this have sound design that matches the visual quality?
questions.answer: Not yet designed. The demo currently has no audio beyond footsteps. Wind/ambient audio would significantly enhance the canyon experience.

questions.question: Can the community extend or modify this?
questions.answer: The educational content is data-driven (JSON prompt lists). Modders can add new observations without touching code. The canyon terrain itself is procedurally generated and not easily moddable.

questions.question: Can this be translated without breaking?
questions.answer: Yes. The educational prompts are text strings in Python modules. They can be extracted to .json for translation. No hardcoded UI text.

questions.question: Does this feature need sub-features, or is it detailed enough at this level?
questions.answer: Zoom in complete. 5 sub-features cover all aspects. No deeper zoom needed at this level.

questions.question: Are there sibling features missing at this level of the tree?
questions.answer: Complete at this level. The 5 sub-features are the right decomposition.

questions.question: Is the parent feature complete enough to support this?
questions.answer: No parent. This is a root-level feature.

questions.question: Should this be built before or after its siblings?
questions.answer: Highest priority — this is the demo that sells the game.

questions.question: Does this block other features, or do others block this?
questions.answer: Blocked by nothing. All sub-features are designed.

questions.question: Can this feature be verified by sleepwalker beat tests?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can walk through this feature and verify state changes.

questions.question: Does this feature have automated regression tests?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.

questions.question: What are the edge cases and failure modes?
questions.answer: Edge cases include: network interruption, empty state, concurrent access, corrupted data. Documented in threat model.

questions.question: Can this feature be tested in isolation (unit test)?
questions.answer: Partially. Python modules have unit tests. UE5 Blueprint/C++ needs automated test framework.

questions.question: Is there a visual/performance baseline for regression detection?
questions.answer: Not yet. Needs MCP screenshot baseline + SSIM comparison for visual regression.
